recipes.name: Canned Spiced Pickled Beets
ingredients_raw: 6 1-quart canning jars with lids and rings

steps.text: Combine white vinegar, sugar, water, cinnamon, salt, and cloves in a large pot; bring to a boil and stir until sugar has dissolved. Stir in beets and simmer until tender, 15 to 20 minutes.

Meanwhile, inspect six 1-quart jars for cracks and rings for rust, discarding any defective ones. Immerse in simmering water until beets are ready. Wash new, unused lids and rings in warm soapy water.

Pack sliced beets into hot, sterilized jars, using a slotted spoon, then pour in beet liquid filling to within ¼ inch of tops. Run a clean knife or thin spatula around insides of jars to remove any air bubbles. Wipe rims with a moist paper towel to remove any residue. Top with lids and screw rings on tightly.

Place a rack in the bottom of a large stockpot and fill halfway with water. Bring to a boil and lower jars 2 inches apart into the boiling water using a holder. Pour in more boiling water to cover jars by at least 1 inch. Bring to a rolling boil, cover, and process for 30 minutes.

Remove jars from the stockpot and place onto a cloth-covered or wood surface, several inches apart, until cool. Press centers of lids with a finger to ensure lids do not move up or down. Remove rings for storage and store in a cool, dark area.

raw_recipe.headline: Canned Spiced Pickled Beets
raw_recipe.description: This recipe for canned spiced pickled beets with cinnamon and clove yields 6 quarts. Don't throw away the juice; use it to make pickled beet eggs.

review.reviewBody: while pickled beets are not everyone's favorite, this recipe ought to be a pickled-beet-fan's favorite! Very easy and just the right amount of spices.

I had to combine a couple recipes to make these perfect so reviewing this exact recipe isn't totally accurate. However, it's a great place to keeps notes for next time. Here's what I did. I didn't slice them because I like bite size small or quartered beets. Then I doubled the brine because I wanted 12 to 14 pint jars. That doubled the cinnamon and it looked like WAY to much so I took over half of it out. I added a handful of whole cloves to the brine (not ground) and one to each jar. When the brine was done, I could've drank it it was so delicious! In the end, I had a ton of brine left and think I could've gotten away with a single batch for my 13 pints. These are the best pickled beets I've ever had!!! (sorry mom).

Just finished eating the last of ten pints I made several months ago and must say that this recipe is as good as it is easy. But you can save yourself the hassle and work of using fresh beets. I used canned sliced beets (63 cents/can) and found that one can of sliced beets neatly fit into a one pint jar. Have the hot brine (per recipe) ready. Drain off the beet liquid from each can and pour the beets into sterilized jars. Ladle the hot brine into the jars, then seal and process. Easy peasy!

Really excellent recipe! A friend gave me a bag of beets and I decided to try my hand at pickling them. I am so glad I tried this recipe, it was just what I wanted. The only adjustment that I made was to used apple cider vinegar for half of the vinegar. I liked the bite it gave to the pickles. I stored them in a gallon pickle jar in the fridge, cause I do not think they will last long. If you like pickled beets, you will love this recipe!

I used about 6#'s of beets and yielded 7 pints. I made the full brine recipe and didn't have much leftover, (I kept the beets whole or in large chunks). Instead of ground cinnamon I added 3 cinnamon sticks to the brine and removed them just before canning. I love how these turned out. Delicious!

I wish I could give this more than 5 stars! 10 would be more like it! I love pickled beets, but hate paying the price the store asks for...and it's such a small jar. Well, no more store bought beets for me. This recipe yielded much more for me, but I did use a few more beets, probably about 18lbs.? Anyway, I got 4 quart jars and 6-7 pint sized jars. Gave them for part of my food basket I give to each family member, along with jams and preserves that I've canned in the summer. Everyone loves these beets! They are well spiced and flavorful. I did reduce the salt to 1 T. to avoid the excessive saltiness that the other reviewers complained about. I will make this each summer/fall when beets are in season.
Made it with fresh orange and red beets in the instapot. They are delicious.
Just tried this recipe with Golden Beets and 3 cups of sugar. Very good recipe.

i'm not a beet lover but my husband is so when we came into a couple of bundles of beets i thought i'd surprise him and try to pickle him some. well all i can say is wow. these are so good that i had to sit down and write my review right away. i scaled the recipe down to 9 servings and was alittle short on vinegar but with some minor adjustments they came out perfect. i didn't try the beets themselves but the juice was awesome. i got 3 pint jars and my husband is already trying to hide them so no one else can have any. this is definately a keeper and i will be doing them again.

Awesome! I added a bit less sugar than asked for, added a couple of teaspoons of cinnamon. And some sliced red onion. We made them for family Christmas gifts this year and added a pretty label and cloth top. It made 7 large almost full jars. I added a touch of water at the end to each jar. Hopefully they will be delish. The one or 2 we taste tested were fab!
Didn’t do the canning part but made 4 lbs of deliciousness. Would definitely do again.

My MIL taught me how to can and I’ve canned everything from green beans to my own spaghetti sauce and chili base. This recipe is similar to a recipe my MIL gave me, but hers used whole cloves and included mace and nutmeg. I’ve used her recipe for nearly 50 yrs.

Followed the recipe exactly, using the 1/2x feature. I had about 6 lbs of beets, and it made 3 pints and a slightly smaller jar. The recipe was very easy to follow… the time consuming part is prepping the beats, but it is worth the time because these are delicious!

A simple -Heirloom delight- the spiced juice from simply boiling beets can be used to make sauces & Syrups for most any dish needing a sweet/colorful twist - a versatile gift to any pallet - the heart -health benefits are over the top! Naturally sugar sweet - no white sugar necessary - Mange' Bella~

I have been using this recipe well over 30 years and am pleased to say it's as good now as it was way back in the day. I'm not one for exact measurements but try to be as close as I can considering I don't own a kitchen scale , I still use the old plastic measuring spoons and cups. I always try to stay close when it comes to super measurements however I favor being a bit on the heavy side. That's why my family and friends love my pickled beets and that's why I always run out of them prior to the next year's garden bounty. Thank you so much for all of your 5star recipes that I make throughout the seasons. Keep the great recipes coming. Ponytailbill1.
I did not add the cinnamon but it was still great.
Just made a batch following the recipe and I’m very pleased with results; so much so that I’m off to the farm for more beets to process! These will go fast!

I cooked my beets before peeling and slicing them; put them in hot sterilized jars and filled with the hot brine I prepared separately. I used six pounds of beets and made the entire brine recipe minus about 1/2 cup of the sugar. The brine is delicious so I'm sure the beets will be. This yielded six and a half pints. They are in the water bath now.
Everyone loves these! Even those who don't even like beets. I use Apple Cider Vinegar instead of White and also add in a little Nutmeg.
